title: Dedicated load-store address generation path
motivation:
The latest timing report identifies the path to dmem outputs through
forwarding and the shared EX ALU as the limiting path. Memory operations
need only a base-plus-immediate address, but currently traverse the general
ALU result selection shared with arithmetic and M-extension operations.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a dedicated address-generation adder in EX for load/store effective
addresses and carry its result in the EX/MEM bundle. Route dmem address,
alignment checks, byte-lane selection, and RVFI aligned address generation

should remove the general ALU result selection from the critical path to
the memory interface without adding pipeline latency or changing retirement.

title: Fetch-stage backward-taken branch prediction
motivation: The current core fetches sequentially and redirects only after a branch or jump reaches EX, flushing younger work on every taken control transfer. CoreMark has repeated backward loop branches, so predicting those branches in fetch can avoid many of these bubbles without adding a predictor table.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Predict conditional branches with a negative B-immediate as taken, predict JAL as taken using its decoded target, and predict forward branches and JALR as not taken. Carry the predicted next PC with the instruction through ID/EX and make EX redirect only when its resolved next PC differs from that prediction. This should remove the taken-loop redirect penalty while keeping prediction state-free and preserving misprediction recovery, bus stalls, and retirement behavior.

title: Iterative RV32M divider
motivation:
Timing reports repeatedly show the critical path passing through the EX ALU,
and the current ALU contains combinational 32-bit divide and remainder
operators. Their long compare-subtract chains can limit the clock even when
the measured CoreMark workload rarely executes division.

hypothesis.motivation:
Timing reports repeatedly show the critical path passing through the EX ALU,
and the current ALU contains combinational 32-bit divide and remainder
operators. Their long compare-subtract chains can limit the clock even when
the measured CoreMark workload rarely executes division.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the real DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU combinational operators with one
shared radix-2 iterative divider that performs one quotient bit per cycle.
Hold the divide instruction in EX and stall fetch/decode while it runs, then
retire it with the completed quotient or remainder. Keep the existing
single-cycle path for all other operations and preserve the ALTOPS formal
substitutions. Removing the long divider chain from the timed combinational
datapath should raise Fmax, while the added cycles should have little effect
on CoreMark if division is rare in its measured loop.

title: Adaptive prediction for forward branches
motivation: The current fetch predictor already handles backward loop branches well, but it predicts every forward conditional branch as not taken. Repeated forward branches that are usually taken therefore incur EX redirects on every occurrence. A small per-PC history table can learn those recurring directions while retaining the existing loop heuristic.

hypothesis.motivation: The current fetch predictor already handles backward loop branches well, but it predicts every forward conditional branch as not taken. Repeated forward branches that are usually taken therefore incur EX redirects on every occurrence. A small per-PC history table can learn those recurring directions while retaining the existing loop heuristic.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Keep backward conditional branches predicted taken and direct JALs predicted to their target. For forward conditional branches, use a 64-entry table of 2-bit saturating counters indexed by the branch PC, initialized weakly not taken and updated once when a valid branch resolves in EX. Carry the resulting predicted next PC with the instruction as today, so existing mismatch recovery handles wrong predictions. This should reduce repeated forward-branch redirects without adding predictor lookup to the EX data path.

title: Reset-safe LUT register file
motivation:
After the divider change, the measured critical path has moved out of the
ALU and now starts in the register file before reaching the ID/EX operand
registers. The register file currently resets every data bit, which can
prevent the FPGA flow from mapping its two asynchronous read ports into
compact distributed memory.

hypothesis.motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the register data array unreset and add one resettable valid bit per
writable register. Clear the valid bits on reset, set a bit on each write,
and return zero for an invalid register while retaining the existing
same-cycle write-first bypass. This preserves the visible reset behavior
while allowing Gowin to map the data array into LUT RAM, reducing the
register-file read mux and reset network on the newly critical path.

title: Synchronous block-RAM register file
motivation:
After removing the combinational divider, timing is limited by a path through
ID, EX, fetch, and hazard control that returns to the ID operand registers.
The current resettable register file also exposes asynchronous indexed reads,
which build a wide mux into that path. Moving reads into FPGA block RAM can
shorten the logic between register storage and the execute pipeline.

title: Return address stack for JALR returns
motivation:
Fetch already predicts backward branches and direct JALs, but predicts
returns through JALR as sequential. CoreMark makes repeated function calls,
so return redirects can still flush useful work on the path back to callers.

hypothesis.motivation:
Fetch already predicts backward branches and direct JALs, but predicts
returns through JALR as sequential. CoreMark makes repeated function calls,
so return redirects can still flush useful work on the path back to callers.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a small eight-entry return address stack for the standard RISC-V link
register x1. Predict JALR returns with rd=x0 and rs1=x1 from the stack top,
falling back to sequential prediction when the stack is empty. Push pc+4
when a valid call writing x1 resolves in EX, and pop when a valid return
advances out of EX. Gate updates during stalls so an instruction updates the
stack only once, and keep existing backward-branch, direct-JAL, and EX
mismatch-recovery behavior. This should remove repeated return redirects
without adding a direction-counter lookup to the data path.
